question: Which analyses use the HistFitter framework for their statistical analysis?

answer.text:
Nine analyses use the HistFitter statistical framework.

Named explicitly in the text (and recorded in the graph as statistical_method entities / result_uses_statistical_method assertions):
- 2006.05880 — background from a profile likelihood fit "implemented in the HistFitter framework"; HistFitter also used for CLs 95% CL intervals with Gaussian-constrained nuisance parameters.
- 2011.07812 — "The HistFitter package is used for statistical interpretation", systematics as Gaussian nuisance parameters.
- 2102.01444 — simultaneous likelihood fits performed "using standard minimisation software packages, HistFitter and pyhf".
- 2106.01676 — profile log-likelihood background fit "implemented in the HistFitter framework"; the pyhf combination of orthogonal signal regions was "validated against the HistFitter framework".
- 2211.08028 — background yields estimated per SR "with a profile likelihood fit implemented in the HistFitter framework" (background-only fit).

HistFitter is the tool invoked (via the Baak et al. Eur.Phys.J.C75:153 reference) for the likelihood fits in:
- 2004.14060 — "binned profile likelihood fits [120]" (ref 120 = HistFitter).
- 2009.14537 — "asymptotic profile-likelihood method [91, 92]" (ref 92 = HistFitter).
- 2010.14293 — "background-only fit is used [93]" and "Model-dependent fits [93]" (ref 93 = HistFitter).
- 2307.01094 — "profile likelihood fit [141]" background-only fit (ref 141 = HistFitter).

The entity ids involved are hepkg:method:histfitter, hepkg:method:profile-likelihood-fit and hepkg:method:profile-likelihood-fit-histfitter (plus hepkg:method:pyhf-combination, which is only cross-checked against HistFitter).

question: Which analyses are searches (rather than measurements) whose event selection uses both b-tagged jets and missing transverse momentum?

answer.text:
Among the 28 papers tagged category='search' in the graph, 22 have BOTH a b-tagged-jet object and a missing-transverse-momentum object as selected/reconstructed event objects (entity kinds detector_object / object_definition, joined via entity_occurrence), i.e. their event selection uses b-tagged jets and MET. Examples of the selection content: 2004.14060 (E_T^miss > 250 GeV plus multivariate b-tagged jets), 2012.08600 (pT^miss > 50 GeV baseline with DeepCSV b-jets), 2012.03799 (MV2c10 b-jets + soft b-tags with p_T^miss), 2010.14293 (MV2c10 77% WP b-jets with calibrated MET). The subset where a signal/validation region explicitly requires both objects (predicate region_requires_object) is 2006.05880, 2106.01676, 2106.14246, 2107.12553, 2112.03161, 2209.07327, 2211.08028, 2508.13900.

Excluded searches: 2008.05928 (b-tagged jets but no MET object), 2407.10549 (MET but no b-tagged-jet object), and 2004.01678, 2011.07812, 2012.01581, 2304.08962 (neither).

The search analyses requested: 2004.14060, 2006.05880, 2010.14293, 2012.03799, 2012.08600, 2102.01444, 2106.01676, 2106.14246, 2107.12553, 2112.03161, 2201.11585, 2202.08676, 2209.07327, 2211.08028, 2302.05225, 2307.01094, 2403.01556, 2506.13565, 2508.13900, 2509.22535, 2510.07527, 2511.11853.

question: Which analyses unfold their measured distributions -- that is, correct them back to particle level or truth level?

answer.text:
**Analyses that unfold their measured distributions back to particle/parton/truth (generator) level**

These are the papers in the graph that carry an explicit unfolding method (TUnfold, iterative/D'Agostini Bayesian, SVD, fully‑Bayesian, profile‑likelihood unfolding with Tikhonov regularisation, or bin‑by‑bin migration/response‑matrix correction) applied to a measured distribution, with corroborating text in the source:

| arXiv id | Unfolding used |
|---|---|
| 2001.06899 | TUnfold least‑squares, response matrices, unfolded to particle level (Z+c/b jet ratios) |
| 2103.04956 | Detector‑effect unfolding of differential/STXS spectra with response matrices |
| 2110.11231 | TUnfold regularised unfolding → unfolded differential WZ cross sections |
| 2112.00895 | Cross sections unfolded to the parton level (W+c) |
| 2206.09466 | STXS results unfolded to generator level |
| 2207.12246 | Iteratively stabilised unfolding + SVD unfolding cross‑check (elastic scattering) |
| 2208.12095 | Fully Bayesian Unfolding of the t̄t differential/charge‑asymmetry distributions |
| 2303.15340 | Bin‑by‑bin unfolding to particle level for differential fiducial t̄t |
| 2308.02285 | Unfolding to particle *and* parton levels (W+c) |
| 2309.14442 | Binned maximum‑likelihood unfolding of t̄t b̄b differential distributions |
| 2312.04450 | Profile‑likelihood unfolding (PLU) with Tikhonov regularisation |
| 2401.05299 | Profile‑likelihood unfolding of particle‑level differential t̄tW cross sections |
| 2402.08486 | TUnfold χ² unfolding with Tikhonov regularisation (dilepton t̄t + jets) |
| 2404.06204 | Iterative Bayesian (D'Agostini) unfolding of W/Z p_T spectra |
| 2504.13081 | Combined *unfolded* differential Higgs cross sections (per‑bin generator‑level POIs) |
| 2506.13565 | TUnfold bin‑by‑bin migration correction of the lepton‑flavour‑ratio spectrum |

Two caveats: (i) 2405.18661 and 2604.21670 discuss and *consume* already‑unfolded measurements (they are a CMS programme report and a global SMEFT interpretation, respectively), so they are not themselves unfolding analyses; (ii) mentions of "unfolding" in 2106.14246, 2401.07090 and of "particle‑level" corrections in 2106.01676/2112.03161 are only reference citations or jet‑calibration wording, not unfolding of measured distributions. One assertion in 2408.03744 tags a binned‑ML fit "for unfolding", but no unfolding text exists in that paper, so I did not count it.

answer.text:
Thirteen analyses estimate a background with an ABCD method or an ABCD-style sideband/matrix method over independent regions (asserted via background_uses_method):

Explicit ABCD / ABCD-named variants:
- 2004.01678 — "Modified ABCD estimate" (hepkg:method:modified-abcd-estimate), with Regions A/B/C (hepkg:region:abcd-region-a/b/c)
- 2011.07812 — "ABCD data-driven background estimation method" (hepkg:method:abcd-method), non-isolated → isolated muon extrapolation
- 2012.01581 — ABCD-style ratio method using eight non-overlapping regions A–H defined by three near-uncorrelated criteria (hepkg:method:data_driven_abcd_ratio)
- 2404.06204 — two-dimensional ABCD sideband method with control regions B, C, D (hepkg:background_method:z-multijet-abcd-sideband)
- 2511.11853 — ABCD (matrix) data-driven estimate from control regions in data, applied to DY+jets, ttbar, single top and diboson (hepkg:background_method:abcd_data_driven_crs)
- 2604.27044 — multidimensional ABCD reweighting (CR→SR, data-driven) for QCD multijet

Matrix method over independent (tight/loose, uncorrelated) regions:
- 2006.05880 — fake-factor/matrix (tight/loose) method for FNP leptons
- 2106.01676 — data-driven matrix method for FNP leptons (RJR 3-lepton)
- 2202.08676 — data-driven matrix method for misidentified leptons
- 2208.12095 — data-driven matrix method, single-lepton fake/non-prompt estimate
- 2209.07327 — matrix method for nonprompt SS-dilepton and (extended) multilepton backgrounds
- 2307.01094 — data-driven matrix method for fake/non-prompt leptons

ABCD-style multi-dimensional sideband:
- 2207.00348 — "Double two-dimensional sideband method" (hepkg:method:double-2d-sideband) for the γγ/γj/jj continuum background

Deliberately excluded although their labels contain "sideband"/"matrix": 2008.05928 (smooth BPDF fit to m_Jγ, mass sidebands used only for validation), 2103.06956 (photon-ID BDT sideband control sample replacing simulation), 2206.09466 (Z-peak/sideband extrapolation for Drell–Yan), 2401.05299 (charge-misassignment rate from a Z→ee sideband), 2510.07527 (background from mass sidebands), plus all "matrix-element generator" systematic-uncertainty entries, which are not ABCD/matrix background methods.

question: Which analyses reconstruct a Higgs-boson candidate as a physical object they select on (rather than merely studying Higgs production or decay)?

answer.text:
Thirteen analyses reconstruct a Higgs-boson candidate as a real, selected object (a detector_object/object_definition carrying object_has_selection criteria and/or required by signal regions via region_requires_object):

- 2004.04545 — hepkg:object:diphoton_system, "Diphoton system (H→γγ candidate)", m_γγ ∈ [105,160] GeV (ttH/tH H→γγ).
- 2006.05880 — hepkg:object:higgs-boson-candidate, "Higgs boson candidate (h->bb jet pair, NN-tagged)", NN score above optimised threshold; required by SR^h_1A/1B/1AB.
- 2008.05928 — hepkg:object:largeR-jet, "Large-R jet (H→bḇ candidate, J)", pT>200 GeV, 50<mJ<200 GeV, Higgs-mass window; required by the single/double b-tag signal regions (Z'→Hγ).
- 2103.04956 — hepkg:object:zz_candidate, "ZZ candidate (four-lepton Higgs boson candidate)", 105 < m(4l) < 140 GeV plus isolation/pairing vetoes.
- 2103.06956 — hepkg:object:diphoton_system, "Diphoton system (H→γγ candidate)", leading/subleading photon pT/m fractions and 100<m<180 GeV.
- 2107.12553 — hepkg:object:h-tagged-jet, "H-tagged large-R jet (H to bb)", mass-decorrelated DeepAK8 discriminator; required by the N_H signal regions.
- 2111.08340 — hepkg:object:candidate-jet / hepkg:object:H-jet, "|eta|<2, pT>250 GeV, mJ>60 GeV, 2mJ/pT<1, ≥2 track-jets" (with double-/anti-tagged variants).
- 2112.03161 — hepkg:object:bb_jet, "H->bb candidate jet", pT>200 GeV, two soft-drop subjets, DeepAK8 Z/H→bb tagger working point; required by SL/DL search regions.
- 2207.00348 — hepkg:object:diphoton-system (+ hepkg:object:diphoton-primary-vertex, hepkg:object:higgs-boson-particle-level).
- 2504.13081 — hepkg:object:higgs_boson, "Higgs boson (reconstructed candidate)" (alias "H candidate").
- 2602.18611 — hepkg:object:large_radius_jet, "Large-radius jet (boosted H->bb analysis)", required by the boosted ggH and VBF H→bb regions.
- 2604.27044 — hepkg:object:h-candidate-merged and hepkg:object:h-candidate-resolved (merged AK8 / resolved dijet H→bb candidates), required by the merged high-purity SR.
- 2605.14245 — hepkg:object:diphoton, "Diphoton system (Higgs boson candidate)", required by the H→γγ diphoton preselection region.

Deliberately excluded are papers that only study Higgs production or decay without reconstructing a Higgs candidate object: 2001.06899 (ZH→ννbb̄, selects b/c-tagged jets), 2007.02873 (VH, H→bb, selects b-jets and τ_h), 2004.01678 (H→Z + light hadronic resonance), 2206.09466 (H→WW), and papers whose large-R jet is a W/Z/top rather than Higgs candidate (e.g. 2012.08600, whose hepkg:object:large_radius_jet is labelled "V (W or Z) boson candidate" with a τ21 2-prong requirement; also 2208.12095, 2209.07327, 2211.08028, 2407.10549, 2510.07527, 2604.21670).

question: Which analyses require exactly two electrons OR exactly two muons as alternative selections -- parallel ee and mumu channels, rather than requiring both?

Analyses that define parallel "exactly two electrons" and "exactly two muons" selections (ee OR μμ as alternatives, rather than requiring both):

- 2506.13565 — channels hepkg:final-state:dilepton-0b / -1b / -2b, labelled "ℓ+ℓ− (ee or μμ) + 0 / exactly 1 / ≥2 b-tagged jets", with observables hepkg:observable:dilepton-mass-spectrum ("m_ll spectrum in ee and mumu channels") and hepkg:observable:lepton-flavor-ratio R(mumu/ee).

- 2511.11853 — parallel hepkg:channel:dielectron (e+e−) and hepkg:channel:dimuon (μ+μ−), with matched region pairs CR_2j / CR_2j^ee, CR_j / CR_j^ee, plus CR_b^ee and CR_{b+j/b}^ee (dielectron serving as the ee partner/control of the dimuon sample).
- 2509.22535 — a single 2-lepton channel built from two alternative object selections, hepkg:object_selection:electron_2L and hepkg:object_selection:muon_2L, under the shared hepkg:object_selection:lepton_req_2L "two opposite-charge leptons" requirement.

The strongest, unambiguous cases are 2506.13565 and 2009.14537; 2511.11853 and 2509.22535 also carry explicit ee-vs-μμ parallel selections (in 2509.22535 the 2L channel additionally admits eμ). Note the graph has no dedicated "ee-or-μμ" predicate, so this was reconstructed from co-occurring channel/selection entities and paper text blocks mentioning "exactly two electrons / exactly two muons".

question: Which analyses have a ttZ background and a control region used to normalise that background?

answer.text:
Seven analyses in the graph both (a) include a ttZ / ttbar+Z background and (b) define a dedicated control region whose purpose is to normalise that background (the link is carried by `background_uses_method` assertions pointing at a "control-region normalisation" background_method, plus an event_region entity labelled as a ttZ CR):

1. **2004.14060** – ATLAS stop/all-hadronic tt+E_T^miss search: `$t\bar{t}+Z$ background` → "Control-region-based background normalisation via simultaneous profile likelihood fit", with the CRTTZ region explicitly defined as "Detailed CR definitions for … $t\bar{t}+Z$ (CRTTZ)".
2. **2006.05880** – ATLAS stop → ttZ/ttH: `ttZ background (3-lepton selection)` → "Control-region normalisation via profile-likelihood fit, extrapolated to the SR"; region entity is literally "Control region CR^Z_ttZ for ttZ background normalisation" (plus a VR^Z_ttZ validation region).
3. **2012.08600** – CMS 2-lepton + MET SUSY search: `Z+X background (VZ, ttZ …)` → "Simulation-based estimate normalized/validated in dedicated trilepton and 4-lepton data control regions".
4. **2102.01444** – CMS ttZ/multilepton SUSY search: `$t\bar{t}+Z$ background` → "Data-driven normalisation via simultaneous profile-likelihood fit in dedicated control regions", with CR$_{t\bar t Z}$ (and a four-lepton VR$^{2-body}_{t\bar t Z}$).
5. **2106.14246** is a borderline case: it has a "ttZ-enriched control region (3ℓA-based + b jet)" and a ttX (…ttZ) background, but the graph records the ttX background method as "Direct simulation-based background estimate", so the CR→ttZ normalisation link is not asserted.
6. **2110.11231** – CMS WZ measurement: `ttZ and tZq irreducible background` → "MC-based prediction with free-floating normalization constrained via dedicated control region in combined fit" (CR-ttZ).
7. **2202.08676** – CMS nonresonant multilepton: `ttZ irreducible background` → "Normalization to data in dedicated control regions" (3L ttZ control region, with a ttZ normalization systematic).
8. **2401.05299** – CMS WH(→3ν)/3ℓ analysis: `$t\bar{t}Z/\gamma^{*}$ background` with the "3ℓ ttZ Control Region" and method "Likelihood-fit normalisation factors from control regions" ("Various control regions are defined in order to fit the normalisation of the leading backgrounds … regions enriched in either diboson or $t\bar{t}Z$").

Excluded because their ttZ background is taken from simulation or a parametric fit with no normalising control region: 2009.04363, 2103.04956, 2106.01676, 2107.12553, 2112.03161, 2312.04450 (SR-3ℓ-ttZ is a signal region), 2509.22535.

Six analyses in the graph both include a ttZ (ttbar+Z) background and normalise it with a dedicated control region:

1. 2004.14060 — "$t\bar{t}+Z$ background" normalised by "Control-region-based background normalisation via simultaneous profile likelihood fit" using the ttZ-enriched region CRTTZ.
2. 2006.05880 — background hepkg:background:ttZ-3l normalised via hepkg:object:CR-Z-ttZ ("Control region CR^Z_ttZ for ttZ background normalisation, 3ℓ selection", cross-checked with VR^Z_ttZ) using a profile-likelihood fit extrapolated to the SR.
3. 2012.08600 — background hepkg:background:z_plus_x (VZ, ttZ) estimated from simulation but "normalized/validated in dedicated trilepton and 4-lepton data control regions".
4. 2110.11231 — background hepkg:background:ttz-tzq with "free-floating normalization constrained via dedicated control region in combined fit", the region being hepkg:region:cr-ttz (CR-ttZ).
5. 2202.08676 — background hepkg:background:ttz "Normalization to data in dedicated control regions", region hepkg:region:3l-ttz-cr (3L ttZ control region), with a ttZ normalization nuisance parameter.
6. 2401.05299 — "$t\bar{t}Z/\gamma^*$ background" with "Likelihood-fit normalisation factors from control regions", region hepkg:region:3l-ttz-cr (3ℓ ttZ Control Region).

Excluded because ttZ is taken from simulation/theory with no CR normalisation: 2009.04363 (parametric mumu fit), 2103.04956 (MC only), 2106.01676 ("Direct MC simulation estimate, no control-region normalisation" for ttbar+V), 2106.14246 (ttX from direct simulation; its ttZ-enriched CR serves other components), 2107.12553 (top-quark transfer-factor CR covers ttbar/single top, not ttZ), 2309.14442 (normalised to NLO/NNLO cross sections), 2405.18661 (ttZ is the measured signal; its CRs normalise non-prompt leptons and WZ).

question: Which analyses unfold their measured distributions -- that is, correct them back to particle level or truth level?

answer.text:
Fifteen analyses unfold their measured distributions back to particle/parton/generator level:

- 2001.06899 (Z+c/b jets) — TUnfold least-squares unfolding with a MC response matrix built from particle-level matched objects (hepkg:method:tunfold_least_squares_unfolding).
- 2103.04956 (H→4ℓ) — response-matrix unfolding from reconstruction to fiducial/particle level, repeated with varied matrices to test model dependence.
- 2110.11231 (WZ) — TUnfold regularised unfolding with area constraint; results are "unfolded differential WZ cross sections".
- 2112.00895 (W+c at 8 TeV) — "cross sections are unfolded to the parton level" via acceptance×efficiency C factors (assertions record unfolding target_level = parton).
- 2207.12246 (elastic pp, σ and ρ) — iterative dynamically-stabilised unfolding plus SVD unfolding cross-check, closure test, unfolding covariance matrix.
- 2208.12095 (tt̄ charge asymmetry) — Fully Bayesian Unfolding (FBU) with Protos-based unfolding-bias uncertainty.
- 2303.15340 (tt̄ dilepton differential) — bin-by-bin unfolding using the particle-level ↔ detector-level migration matrix.
- 2308.02285 (W+c at 13 TeV) — explicit "unfolding of measurements to particle and parton levels".
- 2309.14442 (tt̄bb̄ lepton+jets) — binned maximum-likelihood unfolding of differential distributions.
- 2312.04450 (tt̄Z) — profile-likelihood unfolding (PLU) with Tikhonov regularisation and χ² tests on unfolded spectra.
- 2401.05299 (tt̄W) — PLU particle-level differential cross sections with Asimov closure/bias stress tests.
- 2402.08486 (tt̄ + jets, dilepton) — TUnfold χ² unfolding with Tikhonov regularisation, pseudo-data closure/coverage tests.
- 2404.06204 (W/Z pT at 5.02 and 13 TeV) — iterative Bayesian (D'Agostini) unfolding; all reported spectra are unfolded.
- 2504.13081 (Higgs differential combination) — presents combined unfolded differential cross sections (pT^H, pT^j1, Njets, |yH|, |Δηjj|, mjj, τ_C).
- 2506.13565 (high-mass dilepton + b-tagged jets, a search) — TUnfold bin-by-bin migration correction from reconstruction level to generator level for the ee/μμ cross-section ratio.

Borderline/excluded: 2408.03744 carries an "Unfolding" facet tag only via the shared entity "Binned maximum likelihood fit for unfolding" and its text shows no unfolding; 2405.18661 and 2604.21670 merely use/quote published unfolded measurements (roadmap and SMEFT reinterpretation) rather than unfolding themselves; 2206.09466 fits generator-level STXS bins without unfolding; hits in 2106.14246 and 2401.07090 are only bibliography mentions (PHYSTAT, sPlot).

question: Which analyses reconstruct a Higgs-boson candidate as a physical object they select on (rather than merely studying Higgs production or decay)?

answer.text:
These analyses reconstruct an explicit Higgs-boson candidate as a selected physical object (a `detector_object`/`object_definition` entity carrying `object_has_selection` and/or `region_requires_object` assertions), rather than merely studying Higgs production or decay:

- 2006.05880 — `hepkg:object:higgs-boson-candidate` (h→bb̄ jet pair, NN score above optimised threshold; required by SR-h-1A/1B/1AB)
- 2103.04956 — `hepkg:object:zz_candidate` (four-lepton Higgs candidate: 105 < m(4ℓ) < 140 GeV, ΔR and alternate-pairing vetoes)
- 2111.08340 — `hepkg:object:H-jet` / `hepkg:object:candidate-jet` (large-R H→bb̄ candidate jet, pT > 250 GeV, m_J > 60 GeV, ≥2 track-jets)
- 2504.13081 — `hepkg:object:higgs_boson` (reconstructed candidate with mass > 60 GeV, defined by the combined result)
- 2605.14245 — `hepkg:object:diphoton` (diphoton Higgs candidate, 100 < m_γγ < 180 GeV, required by the diphoton pre-selection region)
- 2004.04545 — `hepkg:object:diphoton_system` (H→γγ candidate, m_γγ ∈ [105,160] GeV)
- 2103.06956 — `hepkg:object:diphoton_system` (H→γγ candidate, photon pT/m ratios, 100 < m < 180 GeV)
- 2207.00348 — `hepkg:object:diphoton-system` (two-leading-photon + diphoton mass-window selections; its `higgs-boson-particle-level` object is particle/fiducial level only)
- 2008.05928 — `hepkg:object:largeR-jet` (H→bḇ candidate jet J: pT > 200 GeV, 50 < m_J < 200 GeV, Higgs-mass window) plus `hepkg:object:resonance-candidate` (Jγ system)
- 2107.12553 — `hepkg:object:h-tagged-jet` (mass-decorrelated DeepAK8 H→bb tag, required in the signal regions)

question: Which analyses require exactly two electrons OR exactly two muons as alternative selections -- parallel ee and mumu channels, rather than requiring both?

answer.text:
Analyses whose selection is "exactly two electrons OR exactly two muons" — i.e. parallel, mutually exclusive ee and μμ channels rather than requiring both flavours — are:

• 2009.14537 (ATLAS pp→p(γγ→ℓℓ)p): preselection "exactly two same-flavour opposite-charge Born leptons (e+e− or μ+μ−)", with separate ee+p and μμ+p final states and per-flavour systematics (pileup "ee: 2%, mumu: 3%").
• 2011.07812: displaced dilepton channel "Two displaced leptons (ee, mumu, or emu)", with separate SR-ee/SR-μμ.
• 2201.11585: Z(ll)+jets background "Z→ee, Z→μμ" with independent Z(ee) and Z(μμ) control regions.
• 2511.11853: dimuon signal regions (SR_b, SR_{b+j/b}, CR_j, CR_2j) mirrored by an independent dielectron control channel (CR_b^ee, CR_{b+j/b}^ee, CR_j^ee, CR_2j^ee).
• 2506.13565: categories "ℓ+ℓ− (ee or μμ) + 0 / =1 / ≥2 b-tagged jets", m_ll spectra in ee and mumu separately and the ratio R(mumu/ee).
• 2401.07090: fully separate electron-channel and muon-channel preselections, control/sideband regions and yields.
• 2007.02873: ZH→ℓℓbb requires "exactly two same-flavour loose leptons", the ee and μμ modes being alternative disjoint selections.
• 2012.08600: SUSY search on two oppositely charged same-flavour leptons (ee or μμ).
• 2102.01444: "exactly two signal leptons (two electrons, two muons, or one electron and one muon)" — ee and μμ are alternatives (eμ also allowed).

Papers using only one flavour (e.g. 2009.04363, H→μμ only; 2304.08962, 4μ only) or requiring both (four-lepton final states such as 2103.04956) do not match this either/or pattern.
